title_ar: قناة المجد تستضيف الشيخ الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء في برنامج يتناول مواقف من حياته
title_en: The al-Majd Channel Hosts Sheikh al-Dedew, President of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, on a Programme Treating Episodes from His Life
body_ar:
استضافت قناة المجد صباح اليوم الأربعاء الموافق لـ 07/12/2011 فضيلة الشيخ العلامة محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء في برنامج " يوم جديد"، في حلقة تناقش موضوع مواقف من حياة الشيخ؛ في أسفاره وحفظه وأشعاره..

وقد ناقش موضوع الحلقة الجانب الفقهي والتأصيلي لجملة من آراء الناس حول أسفار العلماء ومخالطتهم للعامة، واستعرض الشيخ – حفظه الله - في ذلك نماذج من أسفار النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهجراته في سبيل الدعوة وإعلاء كلمة الله.

وتكلم الشيخ عن مواقف من حياته في طلب العلم وأسفاره في الدعوة وعن الأجواء التي صاحبت تلك المسيرة العلمية الزاهرة وطريقة الشناقطة في تحصيل العلوم على الطريقة العتيقة وعن مولده مكانا وزمانا، وعن ذكريات الطفولة في طلب العلم والمشايخ الذين درس عليهم..إلى غير ذلك من المواقف التي تستحق الوقوف عندها والاعتبار منها.

كما تعرّض الشيخ لفترة السجن التي مرت به في أيام من أصعب أيام رحلته الطويلة مع الدعوة ومجابهة الظلم والفساد في بلده موريتانيا.

وقد أجاب الشيخ خلال البرنامج على استفتاءات المشاهدين التي تصل من حين لآخر.

ونشير هنا إلى أن مثل هذه الحلقات التي تتناول حياة الشيخ وطفولته سبق وأن استضافته قناة دليل في برنامج مشابه بعنوان " سوانح الذكريات" تعرض المُحاور فيه لكشف النقاب عن طفولة الشيخ ونشأته مع العلم والعلماء ورحلته الطويلة في الدعوة ونشر العلم، وعن مولده مكانا وزمانا، وعن ذكريات الطفولة.

للمشاهدة اضغط هنا:
body_en:
On the morning of today, Wednesday 07/12/2011, the al-Majd channel hosted His Eminence the learned Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, on the programme "A New Day", in an episode discussing the subject of episodes from the Sheikh's life: his travels, his memorisation, and his poetry.

The episode's subject took in the juristic and foundational aspect of a number of people's views about the travels of scholars and their mixing with ordinary people; and in this the Sheikh, may God preserve him, surveyed instances of the travels of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and of his migrations in the cause of daʿwah and of raising high the word of God.

The Sheikh spoke of episodes from his life in the seeking of knowledge, and of his travels in daʿwah, and of the atmosphere that accompanied that flourishing scholarly career, and of the Shinqitis' way of acquiring the sciences in the old manner, and of his birth in place and in time, and of the memories of a childhood spent seeking knowledge and of the sheikhs under whom he studied — and other such episodes as deserve to be dwelt on and to be taken as a lesson.

The Sheikh also touched on the period of imprisonment he passed through, in days among the hardest of his long journey with daʿwah and with confronting oppression and corruption in his country, Mauritania.

During the programme the Sheikh answered viewers' requests for a legal opinion (istiftāʾāt) as they came in from time to time.

We note here, as regards episodes of this kind dealing with the Sheikh's life and childhood, that the Dalil channel had previously hosted him on a similar programme entitled "Passing Recollections", in which the interviewer undertook to uncover the Sheikh's childhood and his upbringing among knowledge and scholars, and his long journey in daʿwah and in the spreading of knowledge, and his birth in place and in time, and memories of his childhood.

flags.arabic: كما تعرّض الشيخ لفترة السجن التي مرت به في أيام من أصعب أيام رحلته الطويلة مع الدعوة ومجابهة الظلم والفساد في بلده موريتانيا
options: translate faithfully and hold for an editorial decision
flags.note: editorial_review, and a mild one. The sentence states as fact that the Sheikh was imprisoned, and frames the imprisonment as part of his confronting oppression and corruption in Mauritania. The imprisonment is a matter of public record; the characterisation of the state is the site's, not necessarily the Sheikh's, and nothing here is presented as his words. Publishing that characterisation in English, on a site under Ummah Collective's name, states it in Ummah Collective's voice about a named government. Translated faithfully — neither softened to 'a period of detention' nor sharpened — and raised so that the decision is taken consciously rather than by default.

flags.context: وقد أجاب الشيخ خلال البرنامج على استفتاءات المشاهدين
options: viewers' requests for a legal opinion (istiftāʾāt)
flags.note: An istiftāʾ is the request that a fatwā answers, and the pair should be kept distinct in the corpus: the glossary fixes fatwā as 'a considered legal opinion' but has no entry for the request side. Option 3 would lose the fact that these were requests for rulings, which matters here because none of the answers survives in this record.

flags.arabic: ونشير هنا إلى أن مثل هذه الحلقات التي تتناول حياة الشيخ وطفولته سبق وأن استضافته قناة دليل في برنامج مشابه
options: render the sense, as done here, treating 'such episodes' as the topic
flags.note: The Arabic sentence does not construe: it sets up مثل هذه الحلقات as subject and then supplies a verb whose object is the Sheikh, so that the clause never resolves. The English renders what the sentence plainly means while keeping the same information and the same order. Recorded because the repair is in the English and not in body_ar, and a reviewer should see that a repair was made.

flags.arabic: الجانب الفقهي والتأصيلي لجملة من آراء الناس حول أسفار العلماء ومخالطتهم للعامة
flags.context: what the episode is said to have covered
options: the juristic aspect and its grounding in the sources
the aspects of fiqh and of uṣūl
flags.note: تأصيل is the tracing of a question back to its roots in the sources, the characteristic move of a usuli. 'Foundational' is thin but keeps it distinct from فقهي; option 2 explains it at the cost of adding words. The record states that this was discussed and gives none of it, so nothing is at stake for a reader beyond the term itself.

translator_notes: A news report on a television interview, written by the site's news desk. Nothing in it is quoted; everything attributed to the Sheikh is the reporter's summary. No ruling is stated anywhere, so the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged — this despite the second paragraph reporting that he treated the juristic aspect of a disputed question, of which not one word survives here.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written; here the body's date and the timestamp agree, both giving Wednesday 7 December 2011.
الشناقطة is rendered 'the Shinqitis' — the scholars of Shinqit, the classical name for Mauritania, whose teaching tradition the style guide's preamble describes.

'A New Day' (يوم جديد) and 'Passing Recollections' (سوانح الذكريات) are programme titles rendered into English; the Arabic is retained in body_ar. سوانح are the thoughts or memories that pass through the mind unbidden, and no English title will carry that exactly.
The closing 'to watch, click here' is the site's navigation furniture; preserved in body_ar, recorded in source_download_link, omitted from body_en.
